class.name: DVTheme
class.brief_description: Resource that centralizes palette, typography, and component style settings for DataViz UI Kit controls.
class.description:
DVTheme packages all configurable look-and-feel data needed by [DVComponent] based controls. A theme carries global colors, spacing, animation timing, and nested style resources for specific component families such as charts, tiles, gauges, and grid panels. Components automatically react to the [signal theme_changed] signal when connected through [DVThemeManager], enabling instant restyling across a dashboard.
Themes can be authored in the inspector or constructed in code before being applied to individual widgets.

signal.name: theme_changed
signal.description: Emitted whenever any property or nested style resource on the theme changes. Components listen for this to refresh their visuals.

method.name: get_token_color
method.description: One colour from the theme's generated palette: a [enum DVColorScale.DVDomain] (background, border, text, graph, accent, status, series), a sub-index within it, and a variant. This is what the components draw with, so use it to make your own UI match them. For [constant DVColorScale.Series] the [param variant] selects the series — [code]get_token_color(DVColorScale.Series, 0, 3)[/code] is the colour the fourth series is drawn in. [constant DVColorScale.Status] uses [param sub] for success, warning, error and info.

method.name: get_contrast_ratio
method.description: The WCAG contrast ratio between two colours, from 1.0 (identical) to 21.0 (black on white). The same rule the theme applies to its own text: 4.5 is the readable-text threshold, 3.0 the one for large text and graphical marks.

method.name: get_text_color_for_bg
method.description: A text colour that meets the theme's contrast target against [param background]. Label your own overlays with this rather than guessing black or white.

method.name: rebuild_colors
method.description: Regenerates every token from the seed colours and emits [signal theme_changed]. Called for you when a seed or flag changes; call it after editing several at once to repaint only once.
